actors.name: Marine Le Pen
actors.role: Leader of Rassemblement National in France
actors.blurb: Marine Le Pen dominates French media coverage after offering to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Brussels to discuss support for Ukraine while asserting her limits on financial aid. She is also actively gathering signatures for her 2027 presidential bid, defending against accusations of fascism in international interviews, and facing protests during public campaign appearances.

actors.name: Javier Milei
actors.blurb: Javier Milei is central to international and regional headlines amid an escalating internal power struggle with his Security Minister Patricia Bullrich, drawing attention from international financial media. He is also sparking political friction by endorsing Spain's Vox leader Santiago Abascal against Pedro Sánchez, advancing plans to suspend primary elections (PASO), and facing fresh legal challenges seeking to reopen corruption probes involving his inner circle.

actors.name: Giorgia Meloni
actors.blurb: Giorgia Meloni remains a primary figure in European conservative coverage as she prepares to travel to Berlin for high-level meetings on Ukraine with the Coalition of the Willing. Domestically, she is launching a major tax policy offensive proposing a flat tax extension while leading national initiatives against gender-based violence and receiving international recognition for Italy's Africa policy.

actors.name: Santiago Abascal
actors.blurb: Santiago Abascal is driving Spanish political news as Vox enters the final stretch of regional election campaigning, holding major rallies in Madrid and Valencia while advocating for national priority housing and anti-immigration measures. Abascal's campaign has received a high-profile boost from Argentine President Javier Milei while facing criticism from left-wing opponents for declining media debate invitations.

actors.name: Jair Bolsonaro
actors.blurb: Jair Bolsonaro continues to generate significant news coverage in Brazil as the Prosecutor-General's Office (PGR) urges the Supreme Court to uphold a 27-year prison sentence against him. Meanwhile, federal police carry out searches in connected investigations into parliamentary funds linked to a biographical film, while the Supreme Court addresses his security protocols and archived digital ban cases.
